newsitem.title: USA: US Senate's Lott to try to meet Barshefsky Monday.
newsitem.headline: US Senate's Lott to try to meet Barshefsky Monday.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said he would try to meet Monday with Charlene Barsefsky, President Clinton's choice for U.S. trade representative, but could not predict when the Senate would act on her nomination.

Lott said South Carolina Democratic Sen. Fritz Hollings had informed him that he wanted to offer an amendment to a waiver needed before Barshefsky can be confirmed, dealing with Congress's authority to review future trade agreements.
"I'm going to try to meet with her again on Monday," Lott told a news conference.
Barshefsky's nomination has been cleared by the Senate Finance Committee.

Before it can be approved by the full Senate, Congress must waive a law prohibiting anyone who has ever represented a foreign government or foreign political party in trade negotiations from serving as U.S. trade representative or deputy trade reprsentative.
"This is a very, very important position. For the Senate to take a couple of weeks ... is not exactly delay," Lott said.

The Mississippi Republican did not say whether Congress would act on the nomination next week or delay a vote until after a scheduled recess. He said he had not taken any position on Hollings' amendment. Hollings' office was not immediately available to describe the proposal.
Lott also said that no time had been set for the Senate Labor Committee to begin hearings on the nomination of Alexis Herman as Labor Secretary.
The nomination of Herman, a White House official, has been held up due to questions about the extent of her involvement in some questionable Democratic fundraising activities.
